alba-0.name: Kenneth MacAlpin
alba-0.era: d. 858; king in the mid-ninth century
alba-0.attire: Wool tunic, linen underlayer, heavy muted green cloak fastened with an Insular silver penannular brooch; modest gold fillet
alba-0.props: Sheathed early medieval sword, small reliquary
alba-0.setting: Timber royal hall near Dunkeld, carved cross visible in rain beyond
alba-0.likeness: Invented mature face; no reliable life portrait. Royal chronology is evidence, while face and staging are reconstruction. Brooch follows surviving early medieval Scottish material culture, not a personal possession.
alba-0.avoid: Modern clan tartan, kilt, plate armour, Viking horned helmet, treating a later royal portrait as eyewitness evidence

alba-1.name: St Margaret
alba-1.attire: Late eleventh-century long wool/silk gown, restrained embroidered mantle, linen head veil and slim circlet
alba-1.props: Small decorated Gospel book held to chest
alba-1.setting: Quiet Romanesque royal chapel interior evoking Dunfermline
alba-1.likeness: Face interpreted, not a verified likeness. Piety and book patronage have textual evidence; Bodleian Gospel association supports the chosen prop. No assertion this imagined gown survives.
alba-1.avoid: Renaissance crown, late Gothic hennin, modern tartan, literal halo mistaken for physical attire

alba-2.name: Malcolm III
alba-2.attire: Eleventh-century mail shirt over quilted tunic; heavy wool cloak, narrow royal circlet
alba-2.props: Simple straight sword and edge of a kite shield
alba-2.setting: Windy Anglo-Scottish border fort with timber palisade
alba-2.likeness: Mature weathered face is reconstruction. The historical warrior king is distinct from Shakespeare's character; identity and frontier career are sourced.
alba-2.avoid: Shakespeare costume, modern great kilt, full plate, oversized fantasy blade

alba-3.name: David I
alba-3.attire: Anglo-Norman long tunic, embroidered collar and restrained mantle; low open crown
alba-3.props: Rolled sealed charter, stone architectural plan suggested on desk
alba-3.setting: Romanesque abbey arcade beside an emerging burgh
alba-3.likeness: Interpretive face, based on twelfth-century royal types rather than claiming a life portrait. Abbey and charter staging evokes documented reforms.
alba-3.avoid: Renaissance scholar costume, spectacles, Gothic building completed centuries later

alba-4.name: William the Lion
alba-4.attire: Late twelfth-century mail hauberk, plain ochre surcoat and wool mantle; uncovered head with modest circlet
alba-4.props: Upright sheathed sword and small wax seal
alba-4.setting: Stone hall associated with Arbroath, early pointed arch
alba-4.likeness: No assured facial likeness; a deliberately individual adult reconstruction. Royal seal/royal biography supports rulership, not exact face or costume colours.
alba-4.avoid: Lion pelt, full fifteenth-century armour, pretending the nickname proves a personal lion garment

alba-5.name: Alexander II
alba-5.attire: Thirteenth-century long tunic and fur-lined blue-green mantle; open crown
alba-5.setting: Border hall with hills beyond, recalling the 1237 Treaty of York
alba-5.likeness: Plausible mature face, not eyewitness portrait. Treaty, identity and dates are documented; setting and garment palette inferred.
alba-5.avoid: Russian imperial uniform or likeness of Tsar Alexander II; modern drawn national borders

alba-6.name: Alexander III
alba-6.attire: Rich mid-thirteenth-century tunic, crimson mantle fastened at shoulder, low crown
alba-6.props: Folded parchment and small royal seal
alba-6.setting: Scottish stone chamber opening onto a distant western sea
alba-6.likeness: Face reconstructed. Later manuscript royal imagery is iconographic context, not a photographic likeness; western-sea setting evokes the settlement of 1266.
alba-6.avoid: Tsar Alexander III, nineteenth-century uniforms, oversized modern Scottish regalia

alba-7.name: Robert the Bruce
alba-7.attire: Early fourteenth-century mail with restrained coat of plates beneath surcoat, weathered cloak; head bare
alba-7.props: One-handed battle axe held low; shield edge
alba-7.setting: Bannockburn terrain with distant Stirling silhouette
alba-7.likeness: Interpretive face. Later statues and skull-derived reconstructions do not establish an exact life likeness; use the historical sites for context only.
alba-7.avoid: Blue face paint, kilt, late full plate, actor likeness, gore

alba-8.name: Marjorie Bruce
alba-8.era: c. 1296–1316; daughter of Robert I, mother of Robert II
alba-8.attire: Early fourteenth-century long fitted-sleeve gown, light veil, narrow jeweled fillet; no sovereign crown
alba-8.props: Small folded family letter, simple girdle
alba-8.setting: Quiet western Scottish noble chamber, stone window and subdued tapestry
alba-8.likeness: Young adult reconstruction; no verified life likeness identified. She was a princess, not a reigning queen: Queen is a game role. HES documents her marriage to Walter and their royal son.
alba-8.avoid: Queen regnant regalia, Tudor hood, romanticized childbirth scene, claim that a later tomb effigy is certain

alba-9.name: Robert II
alba-9.attire: Late fourteenth-century fur-lined mantle over fitted tunic, understated open crown
alba-9.likeness: Older king with silver hair, interpreted facial structure. Written age and succession history support an elderly portrayal; later portraits are not life evidence.
alba-9.avoid: Youthful warrior archetype, Tudor robes, literal sinister caricature from Intriguer role

alba-10.name: Duncan I
alba-10.attire: Early eleventh-century wool tunic, simple woven cloak, mail only at neckline
alba-10.props: Spear upright to side, small plain brooch
alba-10.setting: Northern royal timber hall in cool morning light
alba-10.likeness: Adult face invented; chronology supported, exact appearance unknown. Avoid automatically presenting Shakespeare's elderly victim.
alba-10.avoid: Shakespeare elderly stage king, modern Highland uniform, plate armour

alba-11.name: Donald II
alba-11.attire: Ninth-century dark wool tunic and earth-brown cloak pinned with an Insular brooch
alba-11.props: Simple sword hilt at belt, timber staff
alba-11.setting: Northern timber stronghold, distant coast and rain
alba-11.likeness: Distinct invented face. Thin documentary evidence supports only cautious early medieval reconstruction, not precise costume ownership or eye colour.
alba-11.avoid: Modern tartan, horned helmet, heraldic lion surcoat, castle from later Middle Ages

alba-12.name: Constantine II
alba-12.attire: Early tenth-century muted wool robe, mantle and restrained silver brooch
alba-12.props: Small cross and rolled ecclesiastical parchment
alba-12.setting: Royal assembly near a stone cross, low timber buildings
alba-12.likeness: Reconstructed elderly statesman; no contemporary facial likeness established. Source supports reign, while the assembly staging is artistic inference.
alba-12.avoid: Byzantine emperor Constantine, Roman laurel armour, modern kilt, Gothic script rendered as legible fact

alba-13.name: Matilda of Scotland
alba-13.era: c. 1080–1118; Edith, queen of Henry I from 1100
alba-13.attire: Early twelfth-century Anglo-Norman long gown, fine linen veil with narrow circlet, embroidered mantle
alba-13.props: Small devotional manuscript, folded court letter
alba-13.likeness: Invented adult likeness. Abbey evidence identifies Edith/Matilda and her marriage/regency; this is not Empress Matilda or Matilda of Flanders.
alba-13.avoid: Conflation with her daughter Empress Matilda, Tudor hood, Gothic hennin

habsburg-0.name: Rudolf I
habsburg-0.attire: Thirteenth-century long tunic, royal mantle and open crown
habsburg-0.likeness: Lean older face inspired cautiously by tomb-image tradition; not a photographic reconstruction. Institution records dates and kingship. Never crowned Holy Roman Emperor.
habsburg-0.avoid: Rudolf II Renaissance artist-emperor, Austrian imperial crown of 1602, full plate

habsburg-1.name: Maria Theresa
habsburg-1.attire: Mid-eighteenth-century silk court gown, lace sleeve ruffles, jeweled bodice and ermine mantle; modest powdered hair
habsburg-1.props: Folded state document, crown resting low on table
habsburg-1.setting: Viennese audience chamber with restrained gilded architecture
habsburg-1.likeness: Mature round-featured face guided by Meytens portrait tradition; a new interpretation rather than exact copy. She was sovereign of Habsburg lands and empress consort, not elected Holy Roman Emperor.
habsburg-1.avoid: Marie Antoinette's enormous later coiffure, medieval gown, all crowns merged into invented object

habsburg-2.name: Maximilian I
habsburg-2.attire: Black broad soft cap, rich fur-trimmed robe, Golden Fleece collar
habsburg-2.props: Pomegranate held low, manuscript at side
habsburg-2.setting: Early Renaissance imperial study with alpine window
habsburg-2.likeness: Use Dürer-derived long nose, shoulder-length grey hair and mature profile as portrait evidence; environment inferred. KHM explains propaganda and portrait variants.
habsburg-2.avoid: Giant fantasy armour, powdered wig, identical face to Charles V

habsburg-3.name: Charles V
habsburg-3.attire: Mid-sixteenth-century etched steel armour, muted red sash, Golden Fleece insignia
habsburg-3.props: Command baton, helmet low at side
habsburg-3.setting: Dusk beside military encampment with river and trees
habsburg-3.likeness: Titian portrait tradition informs reddish beard and long lower face; composition newly interpreted. Physical traits treated respectfully, not as caricature.
habsburg-3.avoid: Valois Charles V, eighteenth-century wig, exaggerated jaw, modern medals

habsburg-4.name: Philip I
habsburg-4.era: 1478–1506; Philip the Fair of Castile and Burgundy
habsburg-4.attire: Cloth-of-gold surcoat, dark fur collar, black soft cap and Golden Fleece
habsburg-4.props: Leather gloves and folded dynastic letter
habsburg-4.likeness: National Trust c.1495 panel describes fair shoulder-length hair and court dress. Show youthful adult with those traits; exact face remains painted interpretation.
habsburg-4.avoid: Philip II's ruff and black beard; Rubens later imagined armour treated as from life

habsburg-5.name: Ferdinand I
habsburg-5.attire: Dark Renaissance robe and small cap, fur trim, short pale collar, Golden Fleece
habsburg-5.props: Administrative charter with hanging wax seal
habsburg-5.likeness: Long-nosed mature face from KHM portrait tradition; not Ferdinand I of nineteenth-century Austria. Documented government supports paper prop, not exact reconstruction of a meeting.
habsburg-5.avoid: Nineteenth-century Austrian uniform, brother Charles V's battlefield composition

habsburg-6.name: Philip II
habsburg-6.attire: Severe black Spanish court doublet, white standing ruff, Golden Fleece chain
habsburg-6.props: Folded dispatch and rosary held low
habsburg-6.setting: Austere stone chamber evoking El Escorial
habsburg-6.likeness: Anguissola 1573 portrait supplies pale mature face and short beard; setting is artistic interpretation. Black dress communicates documented court fashion, not moral villainy.
habsburg-6.avoid: Victorian black suit, fantasy assassin props, excessive black eyeliner

habsburg-7.name: Anna of Austria
habsburg-7.era: 1549–1580; Philip II's fourth wife, queen of Spain
habsburg-7.attire: 1570s Spanish court gown, fitted jeweled bodice, white ruff, neatly arranged light hair with pearls
habsburg-7.props: Fine gloves held low, small jewel pendant
habsburg-7.setting: Madrid Alcázar audience chamber, dark restrained backdrop
habsburg-7.likeness: Explicit identity decision: Prado's Anguissola portrait of Ana (1573), not Anne of France 1601–1666. Portrait guides youthful features and coiffure; room and pose newly invented.
habsburg-7.avoid: Conflation with Bourbon Anne, seventeenth-century lace collar or wide panniers

habsburg-8.name: Margaret of Austria
habsburg-8.attire: Widow's dark square-neck gown over plain chemisette, folded linen cap and beaded necklace
habsburg-8.setting: Mechelen library with discreet books and cabinet
habsburg-8.likeness: Conrad Meit's court portrait bust supports adult features and precisely described dress. Regent identity distinguishes her from Margaret 1584–1611, queen of Spain. Setting inferred from court patronage.
habsburg-8.avoid: Childhood betrothal portrait as adult likeness, Spanish queen on horseback, poison bottle

habsburg-9.name: Ferdinand II
habsburg-9.attire: Blackened early seventeenth-century armour, white lace collar, Golden Fleece
habsburg-9.props: Command baton and helmet on ledge
habsburg-9.setting: Imperial chamber with dark curtain and architectural column
habsburg-9.likeness: KHM Georg Pachmann c.1635 portrait provides mature bearded face and black armour. This is the emperor, not Ferdinand II of Tyrol (1529–1595).
habsburg-9.avoid: Tyrolean archduke's 1550s slashed silver doublet, fantasy religious villain iconography

habsburg-10.name: Leopold I
habsburg-10.attire: Late seventeenth-century black armour, lace neckcloth, dark curled full-bottom wig and Golden Fleece
habsburg-10.props: Baton, low sheet of music as secondary detail
habsburg-10.likeness: Benjamin von Block c.1672 portrait guides long face, moustache and wig. Portray distinctive facial structure without mocking exaggeration; music refers to documented interest.
habsburg-10.avoid: Belgian Leopold I, nineteenth-century uniform, exaggerated genetic caricature

habsburg-11.name: Charles VI
habsburg-11.attire: Early eighteenth-century formal coat with rich embroidery, dark curled wig and Golden Fleece insignia
habsburg-11.props: Sealed succession document evoking Pragmatic Sanction
habsburg-11.setting: Viennese council room with restrained Baroque column
habsburg-11.likeness: Institutional c.1720/30 and Auerbach portraits anchor mature facial type. Document prop derives from succession policy; no fabricated readable decree.
habsburg-11.avoid: French Valois Charles VI, Joseph II military austerity, giant modern eagle emblem

habsburg-12.name: Joseph II
habsburg-12.attire: Restrained eighteenth-century military uniform coat, waistcoat, white neckcloth, powdered short tied hair
habsburg-12.setting: Plain working desk in an imperial room, daylight
habsburg-12.likeness: Portrait tradition guides mature broad forehead and unshowy bearing. Institutional evidence supports admission of uniforms at court and administrative reform; details of this desk are inferred.
habsburg-12.avoid: Napoleonic medals, oversized Baroque wig, medieval crown worn with uniform

habsburg-13.name: Mary of Hungary
habsburg-13.era: 1505–1558; widowed queen and governor of Netherlands
habsburg-13.attire: Severe mid-sixteenth-century widow's dark gown, close white cap and dark veil
habsburg-13.props: Folded diplomatic letter and small seal
habsburg-13.setting: Brussels governmental chamber with a subdued sculptural niche
habsburg-13.likeness: Leone Leoni's c.1555 bust commissioned within her dynastic portrait programme informs mature face and widow's silhouette. Do not substitute Maria Anna of Spain (1606–1646).
habsburg-13.avoid: Seventeenth-century Spanish infanta hairstyle, Anne of Austria confusion, generic young queen
